name: Tomb of Jahangir
assumptions: Bay rhythm of five arches, block, five arches is confirmed on two opposite sides in photos; the other two sides are built to the same design.
Podium half side 46.5 m, estimated from photos; the published platform figures conflict.
Terrace 1.3 m above the ground from four steps and a person for scale; the same flight is assumed on all four sides.
The 257 ft (78.33 m) side is read as across the tower faces; the arcade wall stands 0.97 m behind them from a corner photo.
Wall, parapet and block heights fitted to head-on photos; the dossier 6.7 m arcaded storey is taken as the parapet top on the side runs.
Roof tessellation drawn as a simple repeated star on the dossier colour; no clear photo of the roof pattern was available.
Raised square on the roof is 24 m a side and 0.75 m high with a low rail: the dossier confirms it exists, the size and rail are plain guesses, no roof photo was obtained.
Inlay is a simplified painted version of the real panels, keeping their placement and rhythm, not each individual motif.
Verandahs are one bay deep with plain plaster backs; vault forms are simplified and the interior chamber is not modelled.
Slits in the minaret shafts are placed on the diagonal faces from one corner photo.
Minaret shaft widths and balcony heights measured from head-on photos at about 0.1 m per pixel; balcony rail shown as a band with posts.
Finial material is a dark metal by appearance; the garden, sarai and gateways are outside this model.
